newsitem.title: USA: Plains feedlot cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains feedlot cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle markets were inactive near midday Friday, with most feedlots current in their marketings, feedlot sources said.
Tight showlist supplies and higher boxed beef prices resulted in strong packer demand and record large sales for the week, the sources said.

Sales for the livestock marketing week (Friday-Thursday) were estimated by USDA at 196,000 head in the Panhandle, well above the previous record of 155,400 set during the week ended Aug 22 this year. Feedlot cattle had a top price of $72.00 Thursday, up $2.00 from last week.
Showlists next week were expected to be smaller than this week, cattle feeders said.
Cattle next week were expected to be priced at $74.00, with packer bids at $72.00, they said.

Packers reportedly have enough cattle to get them through next week following this week's heavy sales and were not expected to return to the market until Wednesday or Thursday next week, sources said.
